texts.preamble: In The Matter Of Suo Moto Public Interest ... vs The State Of Chhattisgarh on 29 April, 2025 1/9 High Court Of Chhattisgarh At Bilaspur Wppil No. 37 of 2024 In The Matter Of Suo Moto Public Interest Litigation versus The State Of Chhattisgarh Order Sheet 29/04/2025 Heard Mr. Ravindra Sharma and Mr. Apurv Tripathi, Advocates appear as Court Commission Also heard Mr. Prafull N. Bharat, learned Advo General along with Mr. Shashank Thakur, learne Additional Advocate General for the State, Mr. Kumar Wankhede, learned counsel for the respon Nhai and Mr. Ramakant Mishra, learned Dsg along with Ms. Annapurna Tiwari, learned counsel for Union of India. Mr. Ravindra Sharma, learned Court Commissioner has filed a covering memo yesterday i.e. on 28.04.2025 annexing news items of various dates published in different newspapers which is in regard to road accidents which has occurred in the State and has caused loss of life. One of the news Ashutosh Mishra Mishra Date: relates to death of five tribals as a pickup van fell into a 2025.05.02 18:53:59 +0530 canal. He has also filed a data with regard to road accident in the State of Chhattisgarh for the year 2023 and 2024 which shows the total number of accidents which occurred, total number of persons killed and total number of persons injured. In the year 2023, total 13468 road accidents occurred while in the year 2024, the figure was 14853. Similarly, the number of persons killed in accidents was 6166 in the year 2023 while in the year 2024, it was 6752 and the number of persons injured was 11723 in the year 2023 and in the year 2024, it was 12573 and there has been an increase by 10.28% in the number of accidents, 9.50% in the number of deaths and 7.25% in the number of injured. In this regard, he has drawn attention of the Court to page 27 of the covering memo. In The Matter Of Suo Moto Public Interest ... vs The State Of Chhattisgarh on 29 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144468946/ 1 Mr. Sharma further submits that the black spots identified with respect of five Districts namely Raipur, Durg, Janjgir, Sakti and Mungeli have not been cured. He submits that there has been substantial increase in the number of road accidents in District Korba and Surguja by 25.44% and 42.25%. In response, Mr. Thakur submits that since both the Districts Korba and Surguja fall within the coal bearing areas, there is large number of Dumpers plied for carrying coal which can be the reason for increase in accidents. Attention has been drawn by Mr. Sharma to the fact that in the State, some people are using the goods vehicles for carrying passenger which endangers their life. Further, even in the roads which fall within the Municipal limits, because of inadequate lighting facility, accidents are occurred which has to be taken care of by the respective Municipal Councils/Corporations. Mr. Sharma has drawn attention of this Court to page 31 of the covering memo which is in regard to the accidents which occurred because of the stray animals on the road.
